citations.name: requirements.sdk.graph.validation.deterministic_procedures
citations.commentary:
A criterion can also compute its answer with deterministic Rust code.
Its `ValidationContext` exposes the [inspection operations](context-tools.md)
used by the agent's graph tools.
[Searches and outlines](context-tools.md#find-a-node-then-read-its-contents)
help locate code to inspect; tracked reads and edge selections record input
identities and fingerprints, so changes to those inputs can invalidate the
resulting evidence.

rationale:
The `cite` block in `md/requirements/sdk/graph/validation.md` (section Criteria / Execute the criterion with a context) makes claims that the cited declarations support.

- **Deterministic criteria:** The claim that a criterion can compute its answer with deterministic Rust code matches `requirements.sdk.graph.validation.deterministic_procedures`. That requirement says a criterion computes its answer directly from tracked inputs and needs no configured agent.
- **Shared context:** The claim that `ValidationContext` exposes the inspection operations the agent's graph tools use matches `requirements.sdk.graph.context-tools.shared_context`. That requirement says `ValidationContext::inspection()` returns the `InspectionContext`, and the supplied agent uses the same context.
- **Searches and outlines:** The claim that searches and outlines help locate code matches `requirements.sdk.graph.context-tools.search_text.behavior` and `requirements.sdk.graph.context-tools.outline_source.behavior`. The anchor `context-tools.md#find-a-node-then-read-its-contents` exists, as the section "Find a node, then read its contents" in `md/requirements/sdk/graph/context-tools.md`.
- **Invalidation:** The claim that tracked reads and edge selections record input identities and fingerprints, so changes can invalidate the evidence, is supported by `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.inputs` and `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`. The first says `Fingerprinted` retains recorded node-content and successor-set dependencies. The second says `check_inputs` compares each recorded fingerprint with the current state and returns false on a mismatch. `shared_context` also says reads and edge selections made through the context contribute observations.

The passage is explanatory prose, so `cite` is the right role for every citation. It has no `impl` or `test` reference to the same requirements, so no citation is redundant.

text: :::{req} deterministic_procedures
`Criterion::execute` can compute an answer without a configured model provider.
A criterion can compute its answer directly using tracked inputs; deterministic
execution needs no configured agent.
:::{req} shared_context
```rust,ignore
impl<'d, D: Domain> ValidationContext<'d, D> {
/// Borrow the inspection context shared by this criterion's operations.
pub fn inspection(&self) -> &InspectionContext<'d, D>;
`ValidationContext::inspection()` exposes the execution's `InspectionContext`.
The SDK's supplied agent uses that same context for graph-node reads,
outgoing-edge queries, and delivery recording. The application supplies data
through its domain; the SDK supplies and dispatches the tools.
Borrowing the context does not record an input. The reads and edge selections
performed through it contribute the observations described below.
:::{req} search_text.behavior
The SDK's source tools expose `search_text` with a regular
expression and optional scope prefix, context-window size, and match limit.
These correspond to `TextQuery`'s `pattern`, `scope`, `context_lines`, and
`limit`. It uses `Sources::search_text` and returns each match's
file path, line number, and excerpt, together with whether the search
is complete, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.provider_results.search_completeness`.
:::{req} outline_source.behavior
The SDK's `outline_source` tool accepts a project-relative file path and delegates to
`Sources::parse`. It reads one file snapshot and parses those supplied bytes
with the outline library, respecting the project scope under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`.
The tool returns the selectors and kinds in the returned `OutlineContent::outline()`
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. The Rust parse result retains
the file identity and the parsed source snapshot under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.provider_results.parse_snapshot`.
:::{req} inputs
```rust,ignore
// Defined in trust_but_verify::graph.
/// A completed answer and the inputs used to produce it.
pub struct Fingerprinted<D: Domain, O> { /* private fields */ }
impl<D: Domain, O> Fingerprinted<D, O> {
/// The source node this answer concerns.
pub fn source_node_id(&self) -> &D::NodeId;
/// The question's path relative to that source.
pub fn criterion_path(&self) -> &CriterionPath;
/// The review rules used to produce this answer.
pub fn revision(&self) -> &str;
/// Recorded node-content and successor-set observations.
pub fn dependencies(&self) -> &[Dependency<D::NodeId, D::EdgeLabel>];
/// Borrow the completed answer.
pub fn output(&self) -> &O;
/// Take ownership of the completed answer.
pub fn into_output(self) -> O;
`verify` constructs this value from the criterion's completed answer and
execution trace. `load_evidence` reconstructs it from the selected saved record.
Its node identities and edge labels keep their domain-defined types.
:::{req} checking_records
```rust,ignore
// Method on Validator<D>.
/// Compare each recorded input with the current domain state.
/// Return true when every fingerprint still matches, including an empty trace.
pub fn check_inputs<O>(
&self,
inputs: &Fingerprinted<D, O>,
) -> Result<bool, D::Error>;
The method resolves the recorded dependencies through graph operations and
fingerprinting, comparing each with its saved observation. A fingerprint
mismatch returns `Ok(false)` and permits an early return; it need not resolve
later dependencies. An encountered dependency-resolution failure returns an
error.
The method observes the current state that the caller intends to inspect.
Freshness checking has a separate observation scope from criterion execution.
Checked observations enter the new trace when execution explicitly reads
or delivers them.
A checked snapshot can be reused if it still represents the current state.
